gloss: making a living; livelihood; scraping by

definitions.gloss: making a living; livelihood; scraping by
definitions.explanation: A literary term for earning just enough to survive. Literally 'pasting the mouth shut' — having just enough food to eat. Often implies a meager or modest existence.

examples.japanese: {糊口|ここう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{凌|しの}ぐ→凌ぐ：07388_shinogu⟧。
⟦{翻訳|ほんやく}→翻訳：01725_honyaku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{仕事|しごと}→仕事：00480_shigoto⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{糊口|ここう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{凌|しの}いでいる→凌ぐ：07388_shinogu⟧。
examples.english: I'm scraping by with translation work.

examples.japanese: {若|わか}い⟦ころ→〜ころ：03091_koro⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{日雇|ひやと}い→日雇い：14965_hiyatoi⟧⟦{労働|ろうどう}→労働：03785_roudou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{糊口|ここう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{凌|しの}いだ→凌ぐ：07388_shinogu⟧⟦{時期|じき}→時期：03269_jiki⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦あった→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: When I was young, there were times I got by doing day labor.

notes:
USAGE:
Almost always used in the set phrase {糊口|ここう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{凌|しの}ぐ→凌ぐ：07388_shinogu⟧ (to eke out a living). A literary and somewhat old-fashioned expression. The character {糊|こ} means "paste" or "gruel," evoking the image of having barely enough thin porridge to feed oneself.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {糊口|ここう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{凌|しの}ぐ→凌ぐ：07388_shinogu⟧ (to eke out a living)
- {糊口|ここう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{資|し} (means of livelihood)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{生計|せいけい}→生計：13524_seikei⟧: livelihood — a neutral, modern term for earning a living
- {食|く}いつなぐ: to keep oneself fed, to scrape by — a colloquial verb with a similar meaning
